content:
A 'fully funded' headline is not enough to establish what an international applicant would receive. Check fee status, living support, award duration and whether the international tuition difference is covered.

The funding wrappers international applicants meet

Funded PhDs come in a handful of wrappers, and each answers the fee-status question differently. UKRI studentships pay home fees by rule, but most UKRI-funded training grants have historically covered international fee status too — the 2026/27 minimum stipend is £21,805 and the minimum fee drawn is £5,238. CDTs and DTPs pool that money across cohorts and publish per-cohort international allocation; some reserve places, others treat all applicants equally until funding runs out. Salaried systems — German E13 contracts, Dutch cao NU posts at €3,204-4,051 from July 2026, Nordic employed PhDs — have no fee status problem at all because you are staff. Marie Curie Doctoral Networks are the most explicitly international: any nationality, employed for up to four years, with a €4,010 living allowance before country corrections and employer top-ups.

What the advert must state for a funded place to be real: who pays fees, at which status; the stipend or salary amount and its duration; and whether continuation is conditional on progress or budget. The funded-vs-advertised gap is where international applicants get hurt — a 'fees covered' line that turns out to mean home-fee-equivalent only converts a funded PhD into a part-funded one at enrolment. Get the three-line confirmation in writing before you accept.

[[chart:funding-wrappers]][[chart:intl-student-scale]]

Screening a vacancy in ten minutes

Run every advert through the same five-line screen. Line one, money: is an amount stated — a stipend figure, a salary scale or an allowance — and does it match a 2026 reference (UKRI £21,805, cao NU €3,204+, E13 table, MSCA €4,010)? Line two, fees: does the text commit fees for your fee status in words, not implications? Line three, duration: is the funded period stated in years, and does it match the programme length? Line four, eligibility: nationality, degree-at-start and mobility rules — for MSCA specifically, the 36-month residency rule. Line five, dates: a deadline that is a real date. Any blank line is a question for the contact email; two blank lines on money and fees is a reason to move on.

Where the advert passes, verify externally in two clicks: the funder's own page (UKRI, MSCA, the cao NU table, the TdL table) to confirm the amounts, and the department's recent cohorts to see whether international students were actually funded last cycle. Adverts describe intentions; cohort lists show behaviour.

Read the fee coverage carefully

Look for explicit wording about overseas tuition fees, international fee waivers or restrictions to Home-fee applicants. A studentship paying the Home rate may leave a substantial gap for an international student. Ask the funding office whether that difference is covered for your circumstances.

Check living support and duration

Identify the stipend or salary, payment frequency and guaranteed funding period. Separate an advertised current rate from a future rate that has not been announced. Ask about insurance, research expenses and whether the award continues during extensions, fieldwork or approved leave.

Get confirmation before accepting

Ask: Does this award cover my assessed tuition fee in full, and what living support is guaranteed for each funded year? Keep the written answer with the offer. Eligibility to apply, admission and selection for funding are separate decisions, so confirm the package attached to your actual offer.

Use a fee-gap question that gets a precise answer

Ask the funding office: “If I am assessed as an international student, will this award cover my full tuition fee or only the Home rate?” Then ask about stipend duration and costs outside the award. Keep the answer with the offer documents. A listing can be fully funded for one fee category and only partially funded for another. Do not infer a waiver from the words “international applicants welcome.” Those words establish who can apply, not necessarily who receives full overseas-fee coverage.

Read the advert as a set of financial commitments

The phrase fully funded is a starting point for questions, not a complete funding agreement. An advert may name a maintenance payment while describing tuition support elsewhere. It may welcome international applications while paying fees only up to a home-student rate. Neither statement alone establishes what an international applicant would need to pay.

Read the entire advert, linked funding guidance and fee-status information. Make a list of costs covered in writing and leave uncertain items marked as questions. Check the award's academic year: a number copied from an earlier intake may not describe the offer you would receive. If a university states that it covers the international difference, retain that exact confirmation with the award documents.

Use a coverage matrix

Cost or conditionEvidence you needAn incomplete answer looks like
TuitionCoverage for your assessed fee statusFees are included, without identifying the relevant rate.
MaintenanceAmount, payment frequency and funded monthsA stipend is available, without stating its duration.
Research costsProject budget and any student-paid chargesAccess to excellent facilities, without a cost explanation.
Immigration and relocationSpecific support or a clear exclusionInternational applicants welcome, without financial detail.
Completion periodFunded end date and any continuation feesA normal PhD duration, without a guaranteed funding period.

Use this matrix to organise enquiries rather than sending a broad request for more information. A funding office can answer a precise question more easily than an email asking whether everything is covered. If an item is excluded, add it to your personal budget instead of treating it as a minor administrative detail.

An email that resolves the fee gap

An illustrative message is: "I am considering the advertised [project title/reference]. I expect to be assessed as an international applicant. Could you confirm whether the award covers the full international tuition fee for the funded period, or whether a difference would remain payable by me? Please also confirm the maintenance amount and the number of funded months."

Replace the placeholders with the real vacancy information. Fee status is assessed by the institution; your expectation is not a final determination. If the reply points to another office, follow that route and retain both responses. A supervisor's willingness to support your application does not replace the financial decision made by the university or funder.

Test the offer against a realistic budget

For illustration, suppose an award pays all tuition and a maintenance allowance, but does not pay a housing deposit, visa charges or travel. The award can still provide substantial funding while requiring money before the first payment. Ask when maintenance starts and whether the first instalment is paid before or after registration. Keep upfront cash needs separate from normal monthly spending.

Check what happens if the thesis is not completed by the funded end date. Ask about continuation fees, access to facilities and the process for any extension. An extension of academic registration does not necessarily extend financial support. You do not need a worst-case prediction, but you do need to understand the commitment you are accepting.

Before you treat funding as confirmed

Distinguish an application, a nomination, an informal promise and a formal award. Record any conditions that must be met before the funding becomes effective. Do not withdraw other suitable applications solely because someone says you are a strong candidate, unless you have a confirmed offer and have decided to accept it.

Can international applicants receive UKRI-linked funding?

Eligible international applicants can be considered under relevant schemes, but the institution's award arrangements and fee coverage still need checking. Read the particular call and request confirmation of any international tuition difference.

Should I apply if one funding detail is unclear?

You can prepare the academic application while seeking clarification, provided you understand the application costs and deadline. Resolve any financial uncertainty before making a commitment that depends on the missing support.

Reconcile the final award with the advert

When an offer arrives, compare it with the information you collected while applying. Confirm the fee status, amount, duration and start date in the actual award documents. Ask about a difference before accepting rather than assuming the advert overrides the letter. Retain the clarification with the final terms.

Questions applicants often ask

Can international students get funded PhDs in the UK?

Yes. Many UKRI-funded studentships and CDT places accept international applicants, salaried systems in Germany and the Netherlands have no fee-status barrier, and MSCA Doctoral Networks are open to any nationality with a €4,010 monthly living allowance before adjustments.

What must a funded PhD advert state?

Three things in writing: fee coverage and at which fee status; the stipend or salary amount and duration; and any continuation conditions. If the fee line is ambiguous, ask precisely — 'covered' sometimes means home-fee-equivalent only.
